claim: A sector's facade (the wall an opening interrupts) is the commonest picnum among its wall records.
evidence: bloodmap/aperture.py dominant_wall_tile docstring (changed 2026-11-17); the owner, 2026-11-17: 'these ceiling crates doesn't feel right'
knowledge/blood/design/apertures-v1.json was re-measured on 2026-11-19 by tools/mine_apertures.py, which imports aperture.dominant_wall_tile; re-run on 2026-11-26 it wrote the same bytes

Merged 2026-11-26 from dominant-means-by-surface-not-by-record: 'a pass that picks the commonest tile must weigh it by length or area, not by count of wall records: sixteen short crate rims outvoted a hall's plaster and the lintel pass painted crates round the room'
use: Ask aperture.dominant_wall_tile; knowledge/blood/design/apertures-v1.json already uses it. Weigh any census of surfaces by surface (length or area), never by record count.
instead: Count length, not records, and only solid walls: the facade is the one-sided wall weighed by its length; only a sector with no solid wall falls back to its two-sided records. A market hall with sixteen 1,024-long crate rims and 11,776 units of plaster came out as 'crate' by record count, and a lintel pass ran 24,064 units of crate band round it.
